doc.title: Will Shade and Dewey Corley Interview, 1960-05-25

title: Maxine Allison sings her baby lullabies
summary: Maxine sings 'Sleep my little baby coon', and names other songs she sang to her son; she says her son got piano from his father.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Sleep my little baby coon Underneath the big round moon When you're in the tree you're swinging Mammy just can't keep from singing Sleep my little baby coon Hunters like to croon your side Flash of light to find your eyes Don't you weep and don't you cry Just keep still till day goes by Sleep my little baby coon Song The wind's so slow, mmmm, just so
That's nice, we like that. What else did you sing to him?
Sleepytime Gal, this is my answer, terrible. Sleepytime Gal.
Yeah, Melancholy Baby, side by side.
No, no Brahms lullaby, didn't know the words.
Things that were popular around that time. Yes. How old is your boy now? He's 32. 32.

And he got piano playing from his father. He got his piano playing from his father, and his maternal grandfather could play any thing in the world except a piano. Now let's turn it back. It's going, okay.
